title.title: Mossgnome and the Hidden Springs
title.subtitle: a cozy gnome adventure
intro: Deep in The Greenwild, under toadstools as tall as houses, the gnomes of Mossunder keep the woods well.
They mend birds' wings, sing the clover awake, and drink from the hidden bubbly springs that keep every glowcap shining.
But this spring, one by one, the fizzing has stopped... and the glowcaps have begun to dim.
Young Wittle, grab your red hat. Grandpa Femble is waiting at the village green.

quests.title: The Dimming Glowcaps
quests.goal: Talk to Grandpa Femble on the village green.
quests.hint: Grandpa Femble is the gnome with the longest beard, near the middle of Mossunder. Press E to talk.

quests.title: A Glow in the Log
quests.goal: Find the hidden spring in Mossunder.
quests.hint: Look for a fallen log glowing like honey at the east edge of the village. Walk inside it.

quests.title: A Friend with a Bushy Tail
quests.goal: Meet Tansy the fox with Little Toffle and go for a ride.
quests.hint: Little Toffle plays by the path south of the green. Once you've met Tansy, press R near the fox to ride.

quests.title: Into Toadstool Wood
quests.goal: Step through the root arch to Toadstool Wood and find Auntie Luddock.
quests.hint: The root arches stand at the north edge of the village. The swirling one on the left leads to the wood.

quests.title: Springs of the Wood
quests.goal: Find both hidden springs in Toadstool Wood.
quests.hint: One spring hides behind a waterfall on the far cliff; another waits at the end of a root tunnel.

quests.title: The Fizzwater Caverns
quests.goal: Meet Uncle Plupkin and find both springs in Fizzwater Caverns.
quests.hint: Follow the fizzing sound: a mossy cave mound, and another waterfall on the west wall.

quests.title: Footprints in the Mist
quests.goal: Find a spring in Mistcap Marsh, then escape the grumbling dwarf.
quests.hint: When the stomping starts, run for the swirling rift on the cliff behind where you arrived. Ride the fox if you can.

quests.title: The Spore Ring
quests.goal: Bring at least 5 springs' worth of news back to Grandpa Femble.
quests.hint: Talk to Grandpa Femble. The fairy ring west of the village wakes once five springs are bubbling again.

quests.title: The Cold Forge
quests.goal: Go through the spore ring and face Krogbold in Cold Forge of Krogbold.
quests.hint: Walk up to Krogbold beside the great lid and press E. Mushroom spells (Button Lance) are strong against his cold iron.

quests.title: A Lid Lifted
quests.goal: Make peace with the dwarf and uncap the Mother Spring together.
quests.hint: Talk to Krogbold again and listen to him. Kindness opens more lids than hammers do.

start.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: Ah, Wittle! Just the gnome I was hoping to see. Mind my beard, it's had a busy morning.
Have you noticed the glowcaps along the path? They're fading, like candles at bedtime.
Our glowcaps drink from the hidden springs. When the springs go quiet, the whole wood grows dim and sleepy.

options.text: Are the glowcaps going to be all right?

why.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: That's the riddle, isn't it? Last week I put my ear to the Brookside spring and heard... nothing at all.
And something else. Far off, a tink-tonk, tink-tonk, like a hammer on iron. Gnomes don't hammer iron. We grow things.

worry.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: They're stubborn little things, like gnomes. Give them a drink and they'll shine again.
We only need to find the springs and wake them up.

help.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: Take this. My old parchment map. It has a few blank corners, but you'll fill those in.
Most springs are hidden: behind waterfalls, inside mossy caves, under tunnels of roots.
Start close to home. There's a log at the edge of Mossunder that glows from the inside. Peek in.

options.text: A map! Can I keep it?

keep.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: Keep it, draw on it, spill tea on it. Maps like being used.
Press M to unfold it whenever you lose your way.

bye.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: Off you go, then. And say hello to the fox for me, if you meet her.
Hmm... Little Toffle has been feeding a fox, hasn't she.

progress.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: The map is already looking well loved.
Every spring you wake makes the glowcaps a little brighter. Can you see it?

options.text: Tell me about the root arches.

next.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: Press H for a hint any time. The quest log in the pause menu remembers what you're up to.
The arches to the north will take you to Toadstool Wood, then Fizzwater Caverns, then Mistcap Marsh. They open one after another.

arches.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: The root arches were grown by our great-great-grandgnomes. Each one remembers the way to one place.
Walk into the swirl and you'll be there before your hat stops wobbling. To come home, find the swirl on the cliff.

hello.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: Hello to you too, young one. Have a clover. No? More for me.

need_more.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: A dwarf! Stomping through the marsh, you say? Grumbling about lids?
I count your springs and come up short. Wake at least five of them, then come back. We'll need their fizz to open the old spore ring.

ring.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: Five springs singing again! I can hear them from here, Wittle. Listen... fizz, fizz, fizz.
And a dwarf, grumbling about lids. That explains the tink-tonk. Someone has been capping our springs with iron.
The spore ring west of the village was planted for days like this. It leads to the high cold places, where the forge-folk live.

options.text: I'll go and talk to the dwarf.

danger.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: Grumpy is not the same as wicked. Dwarves are like chestnuts: prickly outside, warm inside.
But bring your spells, and keep your hat on tight.

brave.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: I'll wake the ring. Stand back... Oh, it tickles!
Go gently, little one. Find out why, before you decide who's wrong.

go_forge.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: The spore ring is awake. It won't stay patient forever, mind.
Find Krogbold. Ask him why.

after.speaker: Grandpa Femble
lines: You did more than win, Wittle. You listened. That's the hardest spell there is.
Look at the glowcaps! I haven't seen them this bright since my beard was brown.

start.speaker: Granny Pawick
lines: Come here, Wittle, let me look at you. Scraped knees again?
A sip of my clover tea, a pat on the hat, and you'll be right as rain.

heal.speaker: Granny Pawick
lines: There. Good as new, and twice as rosy.
If a critter ever knocks the puff out of you, you'll wake up here in my kitchen. Granny's rules.

tea.speaker: Granny Pawick
lines: Clover, a little honey, and three bubbles from a happy spring. The bubbles are the important part.
That's why I'm worried, dear. My kettle spring went flat last Tuesday.

bye.speaker: Granny Pawick
lines: Off you waddle, then. Mind the puddles.

after.speaker: Granny Pawick
lines: My kettle's fizzing again! I've put the kettle on for that dwarf, too. Everyone's welcome in my kitchen.

nomap.speaker: Master Timble
lines: A map? Grandpa Femble has the good one. Go and ask him, he loves giving things away.
Mine are all half-drawn. I keep running out of edge.

start.speaker: Master Timble
lines: Let me see your map... Oh, lovely smudges.
Each spring you find, I'll mark with a bubble. And some springs show you whole regions when you bathe in them.

reveal.speaker: Master Timble
lines: When spring-steam rises, it draws pictures in the air. Look closely and you'll see every nook of the land around it.
The spring behind the falls in Toadstool Wood does it, I'm sure, and there's another under roots in Mistcap Marsh.

tips.speaker: Master Timble
lines: Waterfalls are thin. Caves have mouths. Root tunnels go further than they look.
And if you hear fizzing get louder, you're getting warmer. Press H if you're stuck.

start.speaker: Little Toffle
lines: Shh! You'll scare her! ... Oh, it's you, Wittle.
This is Tansy. She's a fox, and she's my best friend. Well, second best. After you. Maybe.

options.text: She's beautiful! Can I pet her?
A real fox? In the village?

real.speaker: Little Toffle
lines: She got her paw stuck in a bramble and I unstuck it. Now she follows me everywhere.
Foxes are very good at remembering kindness.

pet.speaker: Little Toffle
lines: Tansy likes you! Look, she's wagging. Foxes don't usually wag.
She's much faster than us waddlers. Hop on her back and hold on to her scruff, gently.

ride.speaker: Little Toffle
lines: Press R next to Tansy to climb on, and R again to hop off.
Don't let her chase butterflies. She always chases butterflies.

again.speaker: Little Toffle
lines: Tansy has been telling me about your adventures. Well, yipping. It's nearly the same.

story.speaker: Little Toffle
lines: Yes! Is it about a dragon?
...A dwarf? A grumpy one? That's even better than a dragon.

start.speaker: Auntie Luddock
lines: Well, if it isn't Wittle from Mossunder! Welcome to Toadstool Wood. Mind the puffcaps, they sneeze.
I've foraged these woods for ninety springs and I've never seen the toadstools droop like this.
There are two springs hidden here. One behind the falls on the far cliff. One somewhere under the old roots.

critters.speaker: Auntie Luddock
lines: The shroomlings aren't wicked, only cross. Their caps get sore when the springs run dry.
Bonk them on the cap with your hat (Space) or cast Button Lance (1). They pop into spores and wander off feeling better.

go.speaker: Auntie Luddock
lines: If you need a rest, sit by any spring you've woken. They're lovely and warm.

again.speaker: Auntie Luddock
lines: Still looking? Listen for the fizz. Walk where the water sings.

done.speaker: Auntie Luddock
lines: Both springs bubbling! Did you see the iron lid lying by the tunnel? Heavy, and stamped with an anvil.
Gnomes don't make lids. Somebody with very strong arms has been busy.
The caverns arch should be open now. Find Uncle Plupkin there. He's lighting what lamps he can.

start.speaker: Mistress Guck
lines: Bzz-bzz, hello, dearie! The bees are cross today. No fizz in the clover means no sweet in the honey.
Here, take my last honey drop. It mends a gnome right up.

options.text: Thank you! Can I help the bees?

help.speaker: Mistress Guck
lines: Wake the springs, and the clover will drink, and the bees will hum. That's how it all goes round.

later.speaker: Mistress Guck
lines: Wise gnome. Honey keeps forever, you know. Bees told me.

again.speaker: Mistress Guck
lines: The bees say thank you. Well, they say bzz. It's the same thing.

start.speaker: Uncle Plupkin
lines: Who's there? Oh! A red hat! Hello, hello. I'm Uncle Plupkin, I light the lamps down here.
Or I did, before the springs went flat. Glowcaps won't glow without a drink.
I found big boot-prints by the cave mouth. Much too big for a gnome. Square-toed, like a dwarf's.

dwarf.speaker: Uncle Plupkin
lines: Dwarves live up in the cold places, beyond the fairy ring. They like iron and fire and not much else.
Mind you, I've never actually met one. Perhaps they like other things too.

gift.speaker: Uncle Plupkin
lines: Then take this, you'll need it. My grandmother's spell: Button Bulwark.
It builds a little wall of toadstools around you. Very good for grumpy things.

bye.speaker: Uncle Plupkin
lines: One spring is in a mossy cave mound. The other is behind the waterfall on the west wall. Follow the fizz!

again.speaker: Uncle Plupkin
lines: Follow the fizz! It always gets louder when you're close.

done.speaker: Uncle Plupkin
lines: Look! Look at my lamps! Every glowcap in the caverns is shining!
I heard stomping in Mistcap Marsh, though. Something big and grumbly. Be careful, and ask Old Gabbin there for help.

start.speaker: Ronny
lines: La-la-laaa... Oh, a listener! Would you like to hear the Spring Song?

song.speaker: Ronny
lines: Fizz in the hollow and fizz in the stone,
fizz where the roots make a tunnel their own,
fizz where the water falls down like a veil,
follow the bubbles and follow the trail!

options.text: That's a map in a song!

map.speaker: Ronny
lines: Clever gnome! Our grandparents sang it so nobody would ever forget where the springs hide.

start.speaker: Old Gabbin
lines: Ahoy, little red hat. Old Gabbin, ferrier of the marsh. Not much ferrying when the pools are this flat and still.
There's a dwarf about. Stomps through here every evening with a lid under each arm, grumbling about the noise.
If he spots you, don't argue with him in the mud. Run for the swirl on the cliff, and argue later over tea.

options.text: Why does he hate the noise?

noise.speaker: Old Gabbin
lines: Fizzing keeps him up at night, he says. But I think he's lonely. Lonely folk hear every little sound.

where.speaker: Old Gabbin
lines: Three springs in the marsh. One under roots, one in a cave of moss, one in a glowing log out east.
When the stomping starts, ride Tansy if she's with you. Foxes don't get stuck in mud.

after.speaker: Old Gabbin
lines: You got away! Well done. He's not a bad sort, I'd wager. Just a grump with cold toes.

start.speaker: Krogbold
lines: WHO GOES THERE? A gnome? In MY forge? Hmph!
I am Krogbold Anvilbeard, smith of the cold stair, and I'll thank you to stop poking at my lids!
Fizz, fizz, fizz, all night long! A dwarf can't think, can't sleep, can't hammer!

options.text: The glowcaps are fading because of the lids.

fading.speaker: Krogbold
lines: Fading? Pah! Mushrooms don't fade. They just... sit there being mushrooms.
Enough chatter! If you want my lids, you'll have to knock the puff out of me first!

talk.speaker: Krogbold
lines: Talk? TALK? Dwarves don't talk, we hammer! ...Well, we grumble. Grumbling is a sort of talking.
No! You'll talk me out of my own forge. Have at you, gnome!

puffed.speaker: Krogbold
lines: Hff... hff... all right, all right. I'm out of puff. You bonk hard for a little fellow.
Go on, then. Gloat. Everyone does, when the dwarf falls over.

options.text: Why did you cap the springs?
I won't gloat. Are you hurt?
You should be ashamed of yourself!

cross.speaker: Krogbold
lines: ...Aye. Maybe I should.
But a cold dwarf with an empty forge isn't thinking about mushrooms, is he?

kind.speaker: Krogbold
lines: Hurt? Only my pride, and that's mostly beard anyway.
...Nobody's asked me that in forty winters.

why.speaker: Krogbold
lines: My forge went cold last autumn. The deep fire went out, and I couldn't light it again.
I heard the springs fizzing, warm and happy, all the way down the mountain. So I capped them, and piped their steam up here.
I thought: what do gnomes need with warm water? They've got each other.
I didn't know about the glowcaps. Truly, I didn't.

options.text: We could warm your forge together.
Come and live in the village!

village.speaker: Krogbold
lines: Me? In a mushroom house? I'd bump my head on every door!
...Though I suppose I could carve some taller doors.

together.speaker: Krogbold
lines: Together? The glowcaps... your sunbeam spells... aye, a forge could burn on firefly-light, if a gnome helped kindle it.
And I'd not need a single lid.
Will you help me lift the big one, then? The Mother Spring's been holding her breath all winter.

friend.speaker: Krogbold
lines: Ready when you are, little friend. Stand at the lid and press E. On three. One... two...

springs.spring1: The log that glows from inside is not just a log.
springs.spring2: Walk where the water sings; it hides a door of spray.
springs.spring3: Crawl under the roots and keep going, past the dark bit.
springs.spring4: A mound of moss with a mouth: something bubbles inside.
springs.spring5: Walk where the water sings; it hides a door of spray.
springs.spring6: Old roots make a tunnel; tunnels go somewhere.
springs.spring7: Follow the fizzing sound into the stones.

general: Listen: the fizz gets louder as you get close to a hidden spring.
Press M to unfold your parchment map.
Ride Tansy with R to cross the marsh faster.
Bathing in a spring you've already found heals you completely.
Critters that are cross can be calmed with a hat bonk (Space) or a spell (1-6).
hints.chase: RUN! Make for the swirling rift on the cliff behind where you arrived!

boss.name: Krogbold Anvilbeard

phases.name: Steam-Puffing Temper
phases.tell: his beard braids start to smoke
phases.vulnerable: to glow when he runs out of puff

taunts: Springs are for forges, not for paddling!
boss.defeat: Krogbold sits down hard on his anvil. "Hff... out of puff," he grumbles.

shouts: OI! Who's been poking at my lids?!
Come back here, you little fizz-finder!
Stop! Hff... gnomes are too quick!
When I catch you, I'll... I'll... tell you off very sternly!

pages: Wittle and Krogbold put their shoulders to the great iron lid. One... two... THREE!
With a sigh like a kettle and a laugh like a brook, the Mother Spring bubbled up into the sun.
All across The Greenwild, the hidden springs fizzed awake, and the glowcaps blushed brighter than ever.
Krogbold warms his forge with firefly-light now. He makes kettles for Granny Pawick, bells for the bees, and taller doors for himself.
And every evening, Wittle rides Tansy to the hollow log, to listen to the bubbles hum.
credits: A cozy gnome adventure generated by n64-suite
Models, textures, music, sound and words made procedurally; nothing copied.

mother.name: the Mother Spring
mother.hide_desc: under the dwarf's great iron lid

reward.text: Every spring in the Greenwild sighs and fizzes back to life.
